method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma' (published 22 October 2025). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12541557). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **Base the diagnosis on an excised node where feasible** (V, A); use a core biopsy only when no node is easy to reach, never fine-needle aspiration, and have an expert haematopathologist review it. Leukaemic-only disease can be diagnosed from marrow or blood.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MCL needs a mature B-cell phenotype** (usually CD5-positive) plus proof of cyclin D1 (protein expression, CCND1 rearrangement, or both); conventional MCL expresses SOX11.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check TP53 mutation status at diagnosis** (IV, A), preferably by sequencing, because immunostaining misses truncating mutations, which are up to 30% of the total. If only p53 staining is available, call it positive at 50% or more.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **High-risk histology is blastoid or pleomorphic morphology, or Ki-67 of 30% or more.** Re-biopsy whenever new treatment is needed, repeating Ki-67 and TP53 testing. (IV, B)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage with CT of neck, chest, abdomen and pelvis plus marrow aspirate and trephine** (V, A). If disease looks limited (stage I–II), add PET-CT and GI endoscopy with biopsies (V, B): PET-CT misses marrow and gut involvement too often.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Skip routine lumbar puncture without neurological symptoms** (CNS involvement under 1%). Screen for HIV and hepatitis B and C, and assess the heart before a BTK inhibitor or an anthracycline.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic, low-risk MCL can be watched:** review every 3 months at first, then every 3–6 months (V, B). In a UK cohort 38% were observed, with a median of about 21 months before treatment. Early targeted therapy belongs only in trials (II, C).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage I without risk factors: observe or give involved-site radiotherapy (24–36 Gy)** (II, B). For intermediate risk or tumour load, consider brief systemic therapy then radiotherapy (IV, B); stage II with high-risk features is treated as advanced disease (IV, B).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fit younger patients (including fit people over 65): R-CHOP with ibrutinib alternating with R-DHAP or R-DHAOx, then ibrutinib for 2 years and rituximab maintenance for 3 years.** (I, A)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Autograft is now optional:** in TRIANGLE, adding ibrutinib without transplant matched ibrutinib with transplant at far lower toxicity, and ibrutinib after autograft adds much infection. Discuss autograft only for selected high-risk patients (II, C).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If no covalent BTK inhibitor is available first line:** rituximab with high-dose cytarabine induction, autograft, then 3 years of rituximab maintenance (I, B). Autograft can be left out after complete response with NGS-confirmed molecular remission (II, A). If ibrutinib specifically is unavailable, a second-generation BTK inhibitor is reasonable despite no phase III data.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Age 65–70 or over, or unfit for intensive therapy:** rituximab-chemotherapy (R-BAC, III, B; or BR, VR-CAP or R-CHOP, I, B), BR plus acalabrutinib (I, B), or rituximab with a continuous covalent BTK inhibitor (I, B; not EMA/FDA approved).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give rituximab maintenance for 2 years or longer** after first-line BR, VR-CAP or R-CHOP.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **VR-CAP spares the T-cell suppression of bendamustine,** keeping future CAR T-cell or T-cell-engager options open, so it may suit high-risk patients.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For very frail patients, low-dose palliative radiotherapy (2 Gy × 2)** can relieve symptoms at diagnosis or relapse.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **TP53-mutated MCL does badly with immunochemotherapy** (median PFS about 1 year). Consider a first-line anti-CD20 + BTK inhibitor + BCL2 inhibitor combination if available (III, B), and offer trials at every stage (IV, B). Fit patients up to 70 with p53 overexpression may get the ibrutinib-containing intensive schedule with or without autograft (II, C).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BTK inhibitor-naive relapse after immunochemotherapy: a covalent BTK inhibitor (± venetoclax) at second line rather than later** (III, B), including CNS relapse (IV, B), where ibrutinib is preferred.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For BTK inhibitor toxicity, switch agents:** acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib cause less atrial fibrillation, hypertension and bleeding than ibrutinib, and switching usually fixes toxicity without losing control.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Relapse on continuous BTK inhibitor once meant median survival of about 8 months.** After BTK inhibitor-containing therapy, options are anti-CD19 CAR T-cells (III, A), pirtobrutinib (III, A) or immunochemotherapy (IV, B); rechallenge with a covalent BTK inhibitor only after prior intolerance or a fixed-duration course (V, C).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Brexucabtagene autoleucel** (ZUMA-2, 68 BTK inhibitor-exposed patients): 91% response, 68% complete, median PFS 25.8 months, but grade 3+ neurotoxicity in 31%, a real problem in older comorbid patients. Liso-cel gave similar responses (83%, CR 72%) with far less severe CRS (1%) and neurotoxicity (9%).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pirtobrutinib** (non-covalent BTK inhibitor) responds less often (49%, complete 16%) but is well tolerated apart from infection and neutropenia; it suits patients unfit for or relapsing after CAR T-cells, or as a bridge when disease moves fast.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid bendamustine before CAR T-cell collection.** Consider allogeneic transplant for younger fit patients when CAR T-cells are unavailable or have failed (IV, B).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow up for life, as MCL keeps relapsing** (V, D): history, examination, blood counts and chemistry with LDH every 3–4 months for 2 years, 6-monthly for 3 more years, then yearly. Do not use PET-CT for surveillance; check TSH yearly after neck radiotherapy.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After CD19 CAR T-cells:** antiviral prophylaxis (aciclovir 200–400 mg or valaciclovir 500 mg orally twice daily) and pneumocystis prophylaxis for at least 6 months and until CD4 exceeds 200 cells/ml. With IgG under 400 mg/dL and serious or recurrent infection, give immunoglobulin (IVIG 400–500 mg/kg every 3–4 weeks). Vaccinate against COVID-19 and influenza from 3 months; other inactivated vaccines wait until 6 months and live vaccines until beyond 1 year.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association and European MCL Network, HemaSphere, 'EHA-EU MCL network guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of mantle cell lymphoma', published 22 October 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541557/, retrieved 2026-09-23
